methodology: Descriptive current-season regular-season production, not scouting grades or a validated forecast. No team-specific overrides. Missing inputs stay unranked; ties share a rank.
Missing positive-exposure values remain missing. EPA is zero only when its underlying recorded opportunities are explicitly zero. Partial metric game coverage is disclosed in each rank’s evidence.

Every metric uses 75% full-season evidence and 25% the team’s last four recorded games (overlapping samples, not independent tests). All roster contributors are included on the team where they played.

Rate estimates shrink toward the league baseline with 40 target/touch equivalents, 100 dropbacks/QB plays or 150 opposing plays. Per-game totals use a three-game prior; OL rushing efficiency uses 60 carries. Small samples therefore cannot dominate through an extreme raw rate.

Opponent baselines use the same positional group’s performance against each opponent in its OTHER games, excluding every game involving the evaluated team. Opponent baselines are themselves shrunk. We remove 35% of the difference between expected opposition and the league baseline; this is a conservative descriptive adjustment, not a causal isolation of talent.

Weight sensitivity shows the observed rank range across the baseline and 200 reproducible ±20% relative component-weight perturbations, with weights renormalized. It tests dependence on weighting choices, not predictive accuracy, sampling uncertainty or every possible weighting.

Score inputs are standardized across eligible teams and clipped to ±2.5 standard deviations before weighting. Click a rank for its raw season/recent values, opponent baseline, sample exposure and score contributions.

WR/TE/RB: 30% yards/game, 25% first downs/game, 15% TD/game, 15% total EPA/game, 15% EPA/opportunity. Efficiency no longer outweighs sustained production; receiving EPA cannot receive a 50% standalone weight.

QB: 60% EPA/play, 15% net yards/play, 15% first-down rate, 10% turnover avoidance, including QB rushing and sacks. OL: 65% sack avoidance and 35% RB rushing EPA/carry; it remains a QB/back/scheme-influenced proxy, not an isolated blocking grade.
Defense is normalized for opposing dropbacks or plays, rather than games alone. DL includes DE/DT/NT/DL/EDGE/OLB labels. Off-ball LB includes LB/MLB/ILB. Generic DB labels remain excluded from CB/S.

DL: sacks, QB hits and tackles for loss. LB: tackles for loss, passes defended, forced fumbles and a small solo-tackle component. CB/S: passes defended, interceptions and forced fumbles. Individual targets allowed, coverage snaps, missed tackles and blocking grades are unavailable here: these remain production indices, not complete position-quality ratings.

Season results do not automatically predict the strength of today’s injury-adjusted starters. Schedule adjustments use all currently available season outcomes; these are not historical point-in-time backtests.
